[{"front":"What are the fundamental limitations that cause single agents to fail?","back":"Single agents face limitations such as context overload, lack of specialization, sequential bottlenecks, and cognitive load, which can hinder their performance on complex tasks."},{"front":"How do multi-agent systems enhance performance compared to single agents?","back":"Multi-agent systems enhance performance through specialization, parallelization, scalability, and information compression, allowing agents to collaborate effectively and produce higher quality outputs."},{"front":"What is the role of the orchestrator in the orchestrator-worker pattern?","back":"The orchestrator analyzes queries, develops strategies, creates specialized subagents, coordinates their execution, and synthesizes results from multiple workers to achieve high-level goals."},{"front":"In what scenarios are multi-agent systems most valuable?","back":"Multi-agent systems are most valuable when tasks are too complex for a single agent, require specialization, involve quality assurance, allow for parallel processing, exceed context window limitations, or are open-ended."},{"front":"What is the significance of context isolation in multi-agent systems?","back":"Context isolation allows each agent to operate within its own context window, preventing information overload and enabling true parallel exploration, which is critical for managing complexity."},{"front":"How does parallelization impact research time in multi-agent systems?","back":"Parallel execution of subagents can reduce research time by up to 90% for complex queries, allowing systems to accomplish tasks much faster than sequential execution."},{"front":"What are the key design considerations for effective multi-agent systems?","back":"Key design considerations include context isolation, dynamic task decomposition, coordination mechanisms, and a specialization strategy that defines domain expertise and tool access."},{"front":"Why is specialization important in multi-agent systems?","back":"Specialization is important because specialized agents with domain-specific tools and prompts can outperform generalist agents, leading to better quality outputs."},{"front":"What challenges arise from coordination in multi-agent systems?","back":"Coordination complexity grows rapidly, requiring careful design of communication protocols, shared state management, task delegation mechanisms, and result synthesis strategies."},{"front":"What trade-off should be considered when using multi-agent systems?","back":"Multi-agent systems typically use 15× more tokens than simple chat interactions, so it's important to ensure that the benefits of specialization and parallelization justify the increased complexity and cost."},{"front":"How do swarm architectures function within multi-agent systems?","back":"Swarm architectures consist of autonomous agents that interact to solve problems through consensus, division of labor, or emergent coordination, allowing them to organically divide tasks based on capabilities."},{"front":"What is the iterative process in the evaluator-optimizer pattern?","back":"In the evaluator-optimizer pattern, one agent generates solutions while another critiques them, enabling quality improvement through feedback and iterative refinement."},{"front":"When are multi-agent systems not ideal to use?","back":"Multi-agent systems are not ideal for simple tasks that can be handled by a single agent, tightly coupled sub-tasks, low-latency requirements, resource constraints, or fixed workflows."}]
